headline: Palantir's chief technology officer says the Pentagon has already swapped out Anthropic's AI models for rivals' with no operational impact.
score_reason: Lowered from the pool score of 6: the interview aired on 11 Oct 2026, before today's window, and our 12 Oct 2026 edition already carried another part of it; the Anthropic replacement claim is new but comes from a company with an interest.
importance_line: Pentagon staff who use the Maven system and Anthropic's rivals are affected most, since the claim suggests the military can switch AI suppliers quickly, but it comes from the chief technology officer of a company whose growth depends on model choice, and the Pentagon has not confirmed it in this report.
summary: The Next Web reports that Shyam Sankar, chief technology officer of Palantir, a US software company whose Maven Smart System the Pentagon uses, said on CBS's Face the Nation on 11 Oct 2026 that the Pentagon has replaced Anthropic's AI models with no operational impact and now uses models from xAI, OpenAI and Google and open-weight models such as Nvidia's Nemotron. His claim comes from the same interview as the Minab school strike remarks in our 12 Oct 2026 edition and follows the Pentagon's halt on Anthropic's products after a dispute over safeguards for military AI, reported in our 6 and 7 Oct 2026 editions.
notes: Full text read from the pre-fetched file. Event (interview) of 11 Oct 2026, so the qa script is likely to hold it as re-dated; the editor decides. Same interview as C05-15 (smoking remark). Our 12 Oct 2026 edition carried CBS News on the Minab part.
